To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quaternion optimal linear filter is a novel continuous-time optimal linear quaternion estimator that combines the exact treatment, under the continuous-time optimal linear filter framework, of the quaternion process noise and the quaternion observation noise, that the Sun vector determination subsystem of Delfi N3xt can deliver a Sun spacecraft line of sight with a 0.2deg averaged equivalent angular error, and that this novel filter is robust to poor initial conditions.
we propose a continuous-time quaternion filter which is robust against poor initial conditions, and we develop an innovative Sun vector determination subsystem.
(1) a novel quaternion estimator is developed, (2) the estimator is validated via Monte Carlo simulations and (3) it is applied to a nanosatellite mission.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel quaternion filter for spacecraft attitude estimation.
the development of a quaternion optimal estimator, which is able to cope with the quaternion process and measurement noise characteristics, as well as with the quaternion degenerate observability.
the attitude determination and control of a nano-satellite in orbit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed filter is a very robust filter, with a good convergence rate, which is suitable for the Delfi-N 3xt mission and beyond.
the proposed filter is more robust to initial conditions than the extended Kalman filter and is more robust to the sampling rate.
this novel filter outperforms the extended Kalman filter in terms of convergence and accuracy, even when the latter filter is tuned.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the quaternion filter proposed in this paper is the most accurate quaternion estimator to date, in the sense of the mean square error of the attitude estimation, and it is robust to poor initial conditions, low sampling rates and to the presence of outliers in the measurements.
we have developed a novel optimal linear quaternion filter, which is able to cope with a quaternion observation model with state-dependent noise.
the proposed filter is able to provide a statistically consistent quaternion estimate, even when the gyro bias is not known.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the maximum information rate approach can be successfully applied to the quaternion filtering problem.

the proposed filter, which is a continuous-time stochastic optimal filter with a quaternion observation model, is able to provide statistically consistent covariance estimates without requiring tuning.
the quaternion state-dependent noises, which are neglected in most of the attitude estimation literature, can be handled via a maximum information approach.
